provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original task, the pattern cells (colour 2) are mirrored about the centre of the 2x2 box (colour 3). The mirroring is done across the horizontal axis, the vertical axis and both together. The result is a pattern symmetric under y -> y0+y1-y and x -> x0+x1-x, where (y0,x0,y1,x1) is the box's bounding box. This symmetry group, {identity, horizontal reflection, vertical reflection, point reflection} about the box centre, is unchanged by every D4 transform. A rotation or reflection of the grid only swaps the two axis reflections and keeps the box centre at the box centre. So the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates for any d4. It finds the box (colour palette[3]) and computes the row and column sums of its extremes. Each pattern cell (colour palette[2]) is then written to its three mirror partners, but only where the partner is background (palette[0]). Writing all three partners from the original cells gives the same set as the archived two-stage process: horizontal first, then vertical on the result. If the input already shows all four copies, nothing changes.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the palette is a bijection, so background, pattern and box colours stay distinct. It assumes background is palette[0], which matches the generator's default background of colour 0. Partner cells outside the grid are skipped; the generator's placement bounds never produce such cells. If no box-coloured cell is present, the input is returned unchanged. I found no contradictions between the fixtures and the uniform rule. No tests have been run.
